styleSelection.reason: Loose ink and wash: the pen is a visible nib line (opening contours, closing crown and trunk strokes); every wash region is built in layers like precise watercolor so the canopy deepens in steps instead of arriving as one heavy first wash.

HILLS.grass-top.reason: Sunlit slope is a value plane with a crisp edge against the canopy: pale yellow-green wash, then mid layers.

HILLS.grass-wedge.reason: Lit grass wedge between canopy masses: wash plane.

HILLS.grass-band.reason: Narrow lit band: wash plane with one crisp lower edge.

HILLS.grass-lower.reason: Largest light mass: one connected lime wash, then mottling and oak shadows.

HILLS.grass-lowleft.reason: Grass strip beside the lower track: wash plane.

HILLS.path-left.reason: Pale peach dirt track, painted as a thin warm wash with paper glowing through.

HILLS.path-lower.reason: Pale peach dirt track, thin warm wash, crisp edges both sides.

HILLS.path-top.reason: Short pale track at the top edge, thin warm wash.

HILLS.forest-left.reason: Canopy built in layers: pale ground, olive mid crowns, then blue-green darks.

HILLS.forest-lowleft.reason: Darkest indigo crowns arrive last, in glazes over dried mid layers.

HILLS.forest-centre.reason: Large dark canopy mass: mid layers first, dark glazes last, crossing family edges.

HILLS.oak.reason: Focal oak: mid olive crown, dark trunk and limbs drawn in ink at the end.

HILLS.forest-right.reason: Dark crown at lower right with a lit edge towards the meadow.

HILLS.canopy.reason: Everything not claimed by a tighter family (canopy between the masses) follows the same layered build.
